title: Apple has a Mac app coming to make running local AI models easy
lede: Apple is building Harbor, a Mac app that runs open-weight AI models locally as a private inference server and can link several Macs over Thunderbolt 5 to share their memory.

points: The leaker Aaron Perris found the app, which is in private preview under Apple's Claris brand.
Models run on Apple silicon, and data stays on the user's own hardware rather than going to a cloud service.
Harbor finds Macs connected over Thunderbolt 5 and forms a cluster without command-line setup.
Pooling unified memory across machines lets a cluster load models too large for one Mac, or serve more requests at once.
Models can be browsed, downloaded and loaded from inside the app.

points.text: Clustering is seen as the main difference from LM Studio and similar apps, though a reply notes Exo already pools Macs this way.
The Claris brand stands out; some read it as a product for small businesses, likely sold by subscription.
Commenters split on cost: one team would trade a large monthly Claude bill for a Mac Studio, while replies say local models are far behind.
Many welcome a vendor-supported option after setting up Ollama, LM Studio and others by hand, provided it stays lean.
